idiom_name: Bunny headers (seq id / position / size) with a Hash of buffers; Karafka ordered batches
implementation_notes: Ruby's AMQP client Bunny attaches an arbitrary headers map to a published message next to the standard properties, and RabbitMQ delivers a queue's messages in order, so the three fields travel as headers and the receiver keeps a Hash keyed by sequence id. Karafka delivers ordered per-partition batches, but no Ruby framework assembles a group for you, so the release logic is application code; the hand-rolled envelope is therefore the realization.
code_sketch:
x.publish(part, routing_key: 'orders',
          headers: { 'seq-id' => id, 'pos' => i, 'size' => n })

def on_delivery(_info, properties, body)
  h = properties.headers
  buf = (@buffers[h['seq-id']] ||= Array.new(h['size']))
  buf[h['pos'] - 1] = body
  deliver(buf.join) && @buffers.delete(h['seq-id']) if buf.all?
end
pitfalls: Bunny headers are AMQP field-table values: symbols versus strings and Integer versus String must be normalised or position lookups fail.
A consumer that raises before acking gets the message redelivered, so storing a part must be idempotent or a duplicate position breaks the group.
Karafka guarantees order only inside a batch and within one partition; multi-partition groups need an explicit key so all parts land together.
